newsitem.title: INDONESIA: First Indonesian church burning trials begin.
newsitem.headline: First Indonesian church burning trials begin.

text.p: The trial of five Indonesians accused of taking part in a riot last October in which 25 churches and a temple were burnt and five people died began on Monday, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.
Antara said the five appeared in the Situbondo State Court accused of intentionally lighting fires and damaging buildings, charges that carry a maximum penalty of 12 years' jail.

The five, identified only as DS, 27, MJ, 22, ROS, 21, ANS, 30 and IS, 34, were accused of causing massive damage to the Saint Paulus church in their home village of Kilkensari in the Panarukan sub-district, on October 10.
Prosecutors alleged the five accused also damaged a priest's house as well as a gold shop.
The village is near the town of Situbondo about 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second city of Surabaya, where most of the damage was done by a Moslem mob that ran amok.
The crowd was said to be unhappy with the progress of a court case involving a Moslem heretic who was being tried for blasphemy.
Senior military and police figures from the East Java province and district attended the trial as well as a number of leading Moslem leaders from the district.
Some reports said the general public was not allowed to attend the trial for security reasons.

The case was the first of 53 people expected to go on trial for taking part in the riot. Authorities had arrested 54 people in relation to the event, but one man died in custody of a respiratory disease.
